newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM drops U.S. base suits against Okinawa.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM drops U.S. base suits against Okinawa.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday withdrew two lawsuits demanding the governor of Okinawa sign leases for U.S. military bases on Japan's southernmost island, officials said.
The lawsuits, filed by Hashimoto earlier this year, involved leases held by some 3,000 landowners opposed to U.S. military bases.
Hashimoto's move followed a decision last Friday by Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota to take steps to renew the leases for U.S. military bases on the island prefecture.

Following the rape last year of an Okinawan schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen, a case that re-ignited protests against the presence of the U.S. military on the island, Ota had refused to sign orders to renew leases for the facilities.
Hashimoto has pledged renewed efforts to reduce the heavy concentration of bases on the island and set up a five billion yen ($45.8 million) fund to help the economic development of Okinawa.

The subtropical island, some 1,000 km (625 miles) southwest of Tokyo, is home to three-quarters of the U.S. military facilities in Japan and about half of the 47,000 U.S. military personnel stationed in the country, although it constitutes less than one percent of Japan's total land area.
Okinawans have long complained about the heavy concentration of U.S. bases on the island.
In a visit to Tokyo in April, U.S. President Bill Clinton announced consolidations of bases on the island which cut the area they occupy by about 20 percent.
